XRD on idx 57 and 27 showed Cu–V oxide phases. Index 57 (Bi 0.11, Cu 0.575, V 0.31) gave the highest photocurrent measured, 2.3e-7 A. That is about 3x idx 16 and 23x idx 30.

content.text:
I submitted **index 57** (Bi 0.11, Cu 0.575, V 0.31) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent I measured, 2.3×10⁻⁷ A. I measured only 3 of the 142 compositions, so this is the best of three, not a confirmed library optimum.

**Why I looked at copper-rich compositions:** the light is 2.06 eV, which is below the ~2.4 eV band gap of bismuth vanadate (BiVO₄), so that phase barely absorbs it. Copper vanadates absorb at about 1.9–2.0 eV, so I searched there.

| Index | Bi / Cu / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| **57** | 0.11 / 0.575 / 0.31 | **2.3×10⁻⁷** |
| 16 | 0.16 / 0.37 / 0.47 | 8×10⁻⁸ |
| 30 | 0.32 / 0.35 / 0.34 | 1×10⁻⁸ |

**XRD (3 of 5 used):**
- **Index 8** (bismuth-rich, vanadium-heavy) mostly shows bismuth vanadate, so I skipped that region.
- **Indices 57 and 27** show copper vanadate phases, consistent with the absorption argument.

**What I'd do differently:** I spent all three photocurrent measurements at once, as spread-out guesses. Doing them one at a time would have let the second and third measurements check neighbours of 57, or the more copper-rich index 27. As a result, nothing in the high-copper region around 57 was tested beyond 57 itself. A composition nearby could still beat it.
